$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a+b+4c?$
after.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 & -1 \\ 4 & -4 & 8 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼\,\,[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable.

 From the second row, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}=-3.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-(-3)+2{x}_{3}=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4-2{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4-2{x}_{3} \\ -3 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+4c=(-2)+(-3)+4\cdot 0=-5.
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

after.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}Ax={A}^{T}b.
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 6 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 \\ 6 & -4 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & -1 \\ 6 & -4 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -4 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -4 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 3 & -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -4 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-6{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second row, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}=-\frac{3}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-(-\frac{3}{2})+2{x}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1-2{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1-2{x}_{3} \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a-4b+c=-2-4\cdot (-\frac{3}{2})+0=4.
$$

content.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=2 \\ -{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $5a+\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 12 \\ 12 & 24\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 12 & 6 \\ 12 & 24 & 12\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 12 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=1-2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
5a+\frac{b}{c}=5\cdot 1+\frac{(-2)}{1}=3.
$$
